t: This marble statue of Margaret Thatcher stands in the Guildhall. The sculptor Neil Simmons made it after a commission in 1998, paid for by an anonymous donor. It was meant for the Members' Lobby of the House of Commons, among statues of former prime ministers. The House did not allow a statue of a living person there, so it was housed at the Guildhall for the time being. Lady Thatcher unveiled it herself in February 2002. She was prime minister from 1979 to 1990, the longest-serving of the twentieth century and the first woman in the role.
